column7: Refuses a backend token containing bytes illegal in a header value (CR/LF injection) as an OAuth error, and builds the Authorization credential every request relies on.
Hardcodes DestinationPolicy::Configured and wires the OAuth client into with_destination; a wrong policy would silently drop the private-destination and https-OAuth checks.
Handshake path that fixes identity_key=None (shared session bucket) and no extra credentials before delegating; a mistake would bind the handshake to the wrong tenant bucket.
Picks the MCP-Session-Id bucket for a caller identity (the shared bucket only for None), so a wrong mapping would put one caller's calls on another caller's upstream session.
Wires the caller credential headers and identity session bucket into a notification POST; refusal and header building are in build_mcp_headers and finalise_modern_headers.
Runs the OAuth initialize/authorize flow and refuses (AuthorizationRequired or error) when no valid token is obtained, including the non-interactive try_lock refusal.
Stores the message endpoint credentials will be POSTed to, only after resolve_message_url's same-origin check; a mistake would silently drop that cross-origin refusal.
Marks the transport connected with no handshake for an Era::Modern verdict supplied by the caller, so a wrong wiring would silently open the backend-call gate.
Refuses the backend when no shared protocol version exists, rejects a failed initialize, validates the server's selection via checked_selection, and only then sets connected.
Picks the version to retry with and returns None (which legacy_handshake turns into a refusal) when no compatible version exists; a mistake would silently accept or reject a version.
Builds the credentialed, session-carrying listen POST and wires the cancel and frame-cap readers; refuses with 404 when the session cannot heal, while the frame checks sit in read_stream and frame.
Bounds the untrusted upstream stream with SseDecoder FRAME_CAP and drops any note not admitted by watched.admits before it crosses the channel.
Refuses a peer message that is not a notification or whose response id does not equal this listen's request id, dropping it instead of passing it to the hub.
Forces the protocol-version header, strips MCP-Session-Id over any operator header, and refuses a request whose Mcp-Name cannot mirror the method's body field so routing never uses a decoy value.
Sentinel-encodes backend-supplied names so they cannot form an illegal or injected header, and returns an error instead of panicking; a mistake would silently allow header injection.

Refuses non-object params or a non-object _meta before dispatch, so the overwrite of the protocol-version and capability keys with the gateway's own cannot be sidestepped and a caller cannot forge dialect facts.

Replaces any caller-supplied clientCapabilities with only the tasks extension, so the capability facts cannot be forged; the refusal of a task method to a peer not known modern is request_with_task_capability's.

Names the pre-handshake era probe, so request() sends it in the modern dialect and post_and_read binds no session for it; a wrong match would bind another method's session before the handshake decision.
Enforces the pending-event byte bound (via oversized) on an untrusted backend stream, refusing and failing the exchange when one event grows past it.
Refuses a JSON-RPC request frame sent by the backend peer on the response stream and rejects unparseable frames instead of forwarding them.
Stores the max_pending_bytes budget that decode enforces; a wrong value silently loosens or disables the stream bound.
Constructs the decoder with MAX_PENDING_SSE_BYTES and wires it to the stream; omitting it would silently drop the bound (the refusal itself is in decode and drain_events).
Scopes session expiry recovery to the caller's identity bucket and refuses to resend a call (ResendPermission::Denied) after a session heal.
Refuses locally, before the wire, any method outside TASK_CAPABILITY_METHODS or any peer not known to be modern, and never retries a submission.
Builds the resend permission against an empty permitted set so every tools/call is denied resend; a mistake would silently allow resending side-effecting calls (decision in request_with_headers).
Declares that HTTP applies identity headers, which the identity-propagation dispatch gate relies on to let a required backend proceed.
Forwards the caller's extra headers and identity key to send_notification, which attaches the credential; a mistake would send a notification under the wrong identity.
Aborts the OAuth refresh task and terminates every per-identity session with its own credential headers; a mistake leaves an orphan refresher persisting tokens.
Refuses to surface a peer's JSON-RPC error body unless its id equals this request's id, so a stray or replayed reply is never attributed to the call.
Binds a session id the upstream mints to the caller's own MCP-Session-Id bucket (never a shared slot), and never for the era probe, so a mistake would hand one caller's upstream session to another.
